artists.biography:
"The Anchoress is the Welsh multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and author Catherine Anne Davies (aka Catherine AD).
The Anchoress is the stage name of Welsh musician/songwriter Catherine Anne Davies, who also records under the nom de plume Catherine A.D. A self-taught multi-instrumentalist, chanteuse, and singer/songwriter specializing in a heady blend of gothic chamber pop and dark atmospheric art rock, Davies has drawn comparisons to PJ Harvey, Nick Cave, Anna Calvi, My Brightest Diamond, and Kate Bush. She issued a series of well-received independently released EPs before switching over to the Anchoress moniker in 2014 and issuing the single "One for Sorrow.. ~ James Christopher Monger
From March to Dec 2015, Davies performed in Simple Minds' live band, contributing additional guitar and keyboards. She met Jim Kerr through The Dark Flowers collective. She has also performed live with Ed Harcourt at Glastonbury Festival, as well as Martha Wainwright.
Davies has been described by NPR's Ann Powers as "Wales's (much more explicitly feminist) answer to Lana Del Rey."

release_name_discogs: The Art of Losing - Acoustic EP

perplexity.description:
The Art of Losing - Acoustic EP by The Anchoress, released in 2023 on Kscope, offers a stripped-down reinterpretation of select tracks from her acclaimed 2021 album The Art of Losing. This EP showcases a more intimate and reflective side of Catherine Anne Davies’s songwriting, featuring piano-driven arrangements, string quartet versions, and acoustic renditions that highlight the emotional depth and lyrical nuance of the original material. The minimalist production emphasizes the vulnerability and rawness at the heart of the songs, aligning with the EP’s introspective mood.

As a companion to her second studio album, this acoustic release further cements The Anchoress’s reputation for blending dark alt-pop and art rock with deeply personal storytelling. The EP’s focus on reimagined versions of tracks like “Show Your Face” and “Let It Hurt” demonstrates Davies’s versatility as a multi-instrumentalist and producer, while also providing listeners with a fresh perspective on themes of loss, grief, and resilience. Though not as widely reviewed as the original album, the EP was well-received by fans and critics for its sincerity and musical craftsmanship, reinforcing The Anchoress’s standing within the contemporary rock and progressive music scenes.
